query_text: I just finished reading the Expanse novels. Wow. Any recommendations for a new book?

message.content:
Since you loved *The Expanse*, you're probably looking for more space opera with complex politics, realistic physics, and epic scope. Here are some excellent recommendations based on what's coming in 2026 and established favorites that hit similar notes:

## **Immediate Next Reads (Already Available or Coming Soon)**

**James S.A. Corey's new series: *The Mercy of Gods* & *The Faith of Beasts* (2024-2026)**
The same authors! Their new **Captive's War** trilogy follows humanity after conquest by alien overlords called the Carryx. It has the same political complexity and moral ambiguity as *The Expanse*, but with a very different premise about survival under occupation. *The Faith of Beasts* comes out April 14, 2026.

**Alastair Reynolds – *Halcyon Years* (January 2026)**
A noir/murder mystery set in space from the master of hard SF space opera. Reynolds' *Revelation Space* universe is also a must-read if you want that gritty, far-future realism similar to *The Expanse*.

**Gareth L. Powell – *Jitterbug* (March 2026)**
Explicitly pitched as "perfect for fans of James S.A. Corey and Adrian Tchaikovsky." A bounty hunter crew gets caught in a solar-system conspiracy on the fringes of a devastated civilization.

## **If You Want That Expansive Political Scope**

**Adrian Tchaikovsky – *Children of Strife* (March 2026)**
Tchaikovsky is brilliant at alien perspectives and societal collapse. His *Children of Time* series is already a modern classic. This new one promises more of his signature big-idea SF.

**Ann Leckie – *Radiant Star* (May 2026)**
Set in her Imperial Radch universe, this standalone follows a planet that lost its star and must survive underground when the imperial powers decide to annex them. Leckie's work has the same attention to power structures, colonialism, and identity that made *The Expanse* compelling.

**Mahmud El Sayed – *The Republic of Memory* (May 2026)**
Explicitly compared to *The Expanse* in marketing—described as "Arabfuturism" examining what divides and unites civilizations across vast scales.

## **For the Hard SF & Realistic Space Feel**

**Peter F. Hamilton – *A Hole in the Sky* (January 2026)**
First in an ark ship trilogy. Hamilton is known for galaxy-spanning, science-heavy epics. Interestingly, this one is shorter and from a teenage POV, with all three books publishing in 2026.

**Charlotte Robinson – *Mars One* (April 2026)**
A near-future Mars thriller compared to *The Martian* meets *I Am Pilgrim*. If you loved the early *Expanse* books with their realistic solar system colonization, this hits similar notes.

## **If You Want to Explore Established Series Now**

- **Alastair Reynolds' *Revelation Space* universe** – dark, complex, with ancient alien mysteries and human factions in conflict
- **Adrian Tchaikovsky's *Children of Time* trilogy** – evolution, post-humanity, and civilizations rising and falling across deep time
- **Becky Chambers' *Wayfarers* series** – if you want the *character* warmth of *The Expanse*'s crew dynamics with less political thriller

---

Given that you just finished *The Expanse*, I'd honestly start with **James S.A. Corey's *The Mercy of Gods*** to stay with authors you know you love, then pick up **Alastair Reynolds' *Halcyon Years*** or **Gareth L. Powell's *Jitterbug*** for that similar "crew in a broken solar system" vibe.

Sources:
1. https://booksbonesbuffy.com/2025/11/11/26-science-fiction-books-to-read-in-2026-scifimonth2025/
2. https://www.newscientist.com/article/2524887-the-best-new-science-fiction-books-of-may-2026/
3. https://www.newscientist.com/article/mg26935763-100-the-best-new-science-fiction-books-of-2026/
4. https://www.andrewliptak.com/sci-fi-fantasy-books-2026-murderbot-corey-leckie-anticipated/
5. https://www.newscientist.com/article/2521638-the-best-new-science-fiction-books-of-april-2026/
6. https://www.readwithallison.com/april-2026-new-book-releases/
7. https://www.grimdarkmagazine.com/2026-most-anticipated-fantasy-sci-fi-and-horror-book-releases/
8. https://www.grc.com/sn/sn-1008-notes.pdf
